To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) users have a poor mental model of password security, 2) users are not persuaded by security features, 3) users do not understand identity theft, and 4) password managers are not a solution to password security.

(a) users are willing to adopt security systems that are easy to use, but not those that are perceived as difficult to use, and that (b) the adoption of security systems is affected by a number of factors, including the perceived risk of identity theft, the perceived value of the information to be protected, the perceived ease of circumvention of the security system, and the perceived effectiveness of the system.
